fact: Kenya's State Department of ICT and Digital Economy, with Huawei TECH4ALL and Computers for Schools Kenya, delivered digital skills training through the Huawei DigiTruck, as stated by the Principal Secretary.
330 young people in Keiyo South completed the DigiTruck digital skills programme.

KICTANet and partners, with the Nyandarua county government, ran the SheConnects Digital Accelerator trainer-of-trainers workshop in August 2026 for about 100 women and men, each asked to train 50 more, after USAID funding fell through.

Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo Gitau launched the National Digital Literacy Skills Curriculum, developed with KICTANet, ACWICT and the British Council, at the Connected Africa Summit in Diani, targeting 20 million digitally empowered citizens by 2032.
KICTANet says its Strengthening Digital Communities pilot, in regions such as Mandera and Busia, has benefited over 600,000 citizens and the national curriculum builds on it.

The ICT Cabinet Secretary said in mid-2024 that the government's free digital-skills programme had trained 490,000 youths over the past year, with digital hubs being set up in all wards across the country.

The British Deputy High Commissioner said at the 30 October 2026 forum that joint UK-Kenya digital inclusion programmes have reached more than 1.2 million citizens with digital literacy training, including 30,000 young people in basic training and over 10,000 in advanced employability skills, per The Star.

Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura says the Jitume and Ajira digital skills programmes had 182,568 beneficiaries in 2025, up from 41,382 in 2022, with over 280 digital hubs and labs at TVET institutions countrywide, per Kenya News Agency.
